Delta_One_Module_Key_Facts.text: This is Aria. I will read you the Key Facts: one page, everything you must know before you buy. A module is a purchase of the Delta One AI trading engine, for the amount you choose, from one thousand USDT. It is software, paid in USDT on BNB Smart Chain. What it delivers is your module's share of half of each day's trading result, settled at twelve noon UTC. On average, half a percent a day. Not guaranteed.

The maximum is two times the amount you put in, that amount included. Then the module ends. Nothing is paid back separately. Days with no trading profit, or a loss, pay nothing. For the first ten days, every result rebuys: each day's result opens a small rebuy module with its own two times. From day eleven you have the Auto-Rebuy switch. On means rebuy every day. Off means the result goes to your app wallet every day. A Believer keeps the switch on for the whole life of the module, and the module delivers two hundred and twenty percent instead of two hundred. That choice is binding.

From the app wallet you can withdraw any time, five USDT minimum, sent instantly, with only the network gas fee. You are ahead only after you have received more than you put in: at the average, after about two hundred days. You cannot cancel before two times. There are no fees except gas. Commission for introducing others is optional and comes from a separate share; most members earn none. Now the main risks, and please listen to these. You can lose some or all of your money. Nothing is guaranteed by Delta One, a bank or any government. Daily results vary from nothing to several percent, and the average can fall. Your capital is locked until two times. Exchanges, custodians or the network can fail, and USDT can lose its peg. Regulators may restrict this product in your country. Only buy a module with money you can afford to lose entirely. Ask questions before you buy.

Delta_One_Momentum_Plan_Simple_Words.text: This is Aria. I will read you The Plan in Simple Words, page by page. Here is the whole plan in one picture. One: you buy a module. Two: the engine works. Three: you get a share, every day. Four: until two times, then it ends. Five: if friends buy modules too, you get two percent of what theirs make. Every day at twelve noon UTC, the money goes to your app wallet. All numbers are an average. No profit means no money that day. Nothing is promised.

What you buy. Delta One has a trading engine. It is software. You buy a piece of it, and that piece is called a module. You pay in USDT, a digital dollar. The smallest module is one thousand USDT; you can buy more. It is not a bank, and it is not a deposit. The one thousand USDT does not come back by itself. Only pay what you can afford to lose.

What you get. Every day the engine makes money, your module gets a part of it. On a one thousand USDT module that is about five USDT a day, on average. Some days zero. Some days more. Add all the days and divide, and you get about five. Half a percent a day is the average. It is not a promise, and it can change. Nobody can promise a number. Never.

When it stops. Your module pays until you have received two times what you paid. A one thousand USDT module gives you two thousand USDT in total, and then it ends. The first thousand is your own money coming back. The second thousand is rewards. At the average this takes about four hundred days, and slower if the average is lower. After that, you can buy a new one.

The first days, and the switch. Days one to ten are automatic: each day's money buys a tiny new module, and those tiny modules also pay until two times. From day eleven you have a switch. Rebuy: the money buys more modules. Wallet: the money goes to your app wallet. From the wallet you can take money out any time, from five USDT, paying only the network fee.

The Believer. You can choose to be a Believer. A Believer keeps the switch on rebuy for the whole life of the module, and then the module pays two point two times: two thousand two hundred USDT on one thousand. But you cannot change your mind. The switch is locked until two point two times is reached.

Where the money goes. Every one hundred USDT the engine makes is split three ways. Fifty USDT goes to the members: that is the daily share for your module. Twenty-five USDT goes to the plan, which pays the people who brought friends. Twenty-five USDT goes to Delta One. No money made that day? Then nobody gets anything. Not you, not your friends, not Delta One.

Tell a friend. If you tell a friend and the friend buys a module, you get two percent of what the friend's module makes, every day. Say the friend's module is ten thousand USDT and it makes fifty USDT a day. You get one USDT a day. This is small, on purpose. Many friends make it bigger: one million USDT of modules under you would be one hundred USDT a day. Most people never bring friends and get nothing from this. That is okay.

Levels. Your friend is level one. Your friend's friends are level two, and so on. Each level can pay you two percent of what those modules make. How many levels pay you depends on your rank: three levels at the start, up to twenty-one at the top. All the levels together can never be more than forty-two percent of what a module makes.

Ranks. There are seven ranks, named after mountains: Fuji, Kilimanjaro, Matterhorn, Denali, Rainier, K two, and Everest. Seven Summits to Success. Every rank needs three things: your own module, friends you brought, and your team's modules. The first rank, Fuji, needs a one thousand USDT module, two friends, and two thousand USDT in your team, and it is paid on three levels. The top rank, Everest, needs a two hundred thousand USDT module, twenty-one friends, and one million USDT in your team, paid on twenty-one levels. Your rank is checked every day, and only modules that are still running count.

Build wide. A line is one friend you brought, plus everyone under that friend. For a rank, one line can only count for a part: half, a third, a quarter, or a fifth. The rest does not count. So bring many friends. Build wide, like a tree. Not tall, like a tower.

Leaders get the gap. Every rank has a number: six, twelve, eighteen, twenty-four, thirty, thirty-six, forty-two. If your number is higher than the people under you, you get the gap, on every module under them. You are twenty-four, your friend is six, the gap is eighteen, and it is yours. If your friend climbs to twenty-four too, the friend's part of the gap becomes the friend's. So: stay ahead.

Payday. Every day at twelve noon UTC, the money goes to your app wallet, in USDT on BNB Smart Chain. You can take it out any time, from five USDT, paying only the network fee. No money made that day? Nothing comes. That is the rule.

Six rules to remember. One: you are paid on what modules make, never on what people pay. Two: no profit, no money. Three: build wide. Four: stay ahead. Five: modules end at two times. Six: paid every day, in USDT.

Please read this last page carefully. The engine can lose money, and then nobody is paid; this can go on for a long time. Nothing is guaranteed, not by Delta One, not by a bank, not by a government. The money you pay for a module does not come back by itself, and it can be lost. Most members never get money from friends; only their own module's share. Only pay what you can afford to lose. Read the Key Facts, and ask questions first. This was a simple explanation; the full rules are in the Module Product Guide, the Key Facts and the Momentum Plan Guide, and where they differ, the full documents are right.

Delta_One_7_Summits_to_Success.text: This is Aria. I will read you 7 Summits to Success: the whole Momentum Plan on one page. Seven ranks, named after seven mountains, climbing from the left to the right: Fuji, Kilimanjaro, Matterhorn, Denali, Rainier, K two, and Everest. Each mountain shows four things: your own purchase, the people you enrolled, the qualifying volume of your team, and the levels you are paid on.

Fuji: your own purchase of one thousand USDT, two enrollees, two thousand USDT of volume, paid on levels one to three, entitlement six percent, daily cap one thousand USDT. Kilimanjaro: two thousand five hundred USDT, three enrollees, five thousand of volume, levels one to six, twelve percent, cap two thousand. Matterhorn: six thousand, four enrollees, twelve thousand, levels one to nine, eighteen percent, cap three thousand. Denali: twelve thousand, five enrollees, twenty-five thousand, levels one to twelve, twenty-four percent, cap four thousand.

Rainier: twenty-five thousand USDT, seven enrollees, seventy-five thousand of volume, levels one to fifteen, thirty percent, cap five thousand. K two: fifty thousand, twelve enrollees, two hundred and fifty thousand, levels one to eighteen, thirty-six percent, cap six thousand. Everest: two hundred thousand USDT, twenty-one enrollees, one million of volume, levels one to twenty-one, forty-two percent, and a daily cap of seven thousand USDT. Under every mountain you also see the maximum share one line may count for: half at Fuji and Kilimanjaro, a third at Matterhorn and Denali, a quarter at Rainier, a fifth at K two and Everest. Build wide.

At the bottom, how you are paid. Two percent per level: for every contract in your paid levels that produces earnings, each qualified upline receives two percent of that contract's daily earnings, up to twenty-one levels, paid daily, on earnings never on purchases. The maximum matrix payout is forty-two percent of a contract's daily earnings, and the breakage differential pays leaders the gap above the ranks below them. Every figure is an illustration at the engine's average daily result. Results and rewards are not guaranteed, and most members earn no commission at all.

Page two is the ranks panel on its own, larger, so you can read every number with your finger: own purchase, enrollees, volume, max per line, paid levels, entitlement and the daily cap, for all seven summits.

Page three is the payout panel: two percent per level on up to twenty-one levels, the ladder from six to forty-two percent, the daily caps from one thousand to seven thousand USDT, and the six rules. Paid on earnings, never on purchases. No profit, no payout. Balance your lines. Stay ahead. Modules end at two times. Paid daily, in USDT.

Delta_One_Getting_Started_Checklist.text: This is Aria. I will read you the Getting Started Checklist: your first day, step by step. Everything here is done before your first conversation, in order, and the whole list takes one afternoon. Your sponsor can sit with you. Part one, your account. Install the Delta One app and create your account with the enroller link your sponsor sent you; the enroller cannot be changed after your first module is confirmed, so check the name on the screen. Complete identity verification: a government ID and a selfie. Add your own BEP-20 wallet address for withdrawals. Turn on two-factor authentication and write the recovery codes on paper.

Part two, your own module. Decide the size. Fuji needs a one thousand USDT own purchase; Kilimanjaro two thousand five hundred; Matterhorn six thousand; Denali twelve thousand. Buy only what you can afford to lose entirely; the price is not refundable. Decide the Believer question now: Auto-Rebuy locked on for the module's whole life delivers two hundred and twenty percent instead of two hundred, and it cannot be changed afterwards. Not sure? Choose standard. Send the exact amount in USDT on BNB Smart Chain to the payment address the app shows; any other network loses the money. Your module earns from the first 12:00 UTC settlement after the day the payment is confirmed. Then read the Key Facts and the Product Guide, and read the disclosure page of the presentation out loud, once.

Part three, the first eleven days. Days one to ten: each day's result opens a small rebuy module automatically; you do nothing. Day eleven: your first result you can take out. Open the app wallet, see the balance, and make one small withdrawal, from five USDT, to your BEP-20 address, to prove the whole path works. From day eleven onward, set your Auto-Rebuy switch: on means every result rebuys, off means every result goes to the app wallet. You can change it on any day; the setting at twelve noon UTC applies.

Part four, your tools. Download the kit: the presentation, the Key Facts, the Simple Words document, the Product Guide, the Cheat Sheet, the Napkin, the Language Card and this list. Watch the three films once each. Open the Fast Start planner, enter your start date and your own module, and print your ninety-day page. Write your list of fifty names, without judging. Book your first ten conversations for this week, and send each person the Key Facts before you meet.

Part five, before you speak to anyone. Read the Language Card twice, and say its five sentences out loud until they are yours. Read the Rewards Disclosure Statement and keep a copy with you: most members earn no commission at all, and you say so. Know the six rules by heart: paid on earnings, never on purchases; no profit, no payout; balance your lines; stay ahead; modules end at two times; paid daily, in USDT. If you are a sponsor, your job on day one is this list, with your new member, screen by screen. Do not send it. Sit down and do it.

Delta_One_Language_Card.text: This is Aria. I will read you the Language Card: what we say, and what we never say. Carry this. Every sentence a distributor says or writes about Delta One follows it, in person, on WhatsApp, on social media, on a stage. We say purchase, purchase price, a module of the AI engine. We never say deposit, invest, investment, principal, or capital you put in, because a module is a software purchase, and those words are compliance problems. We say rebuy and Auto-Rebuy. We never say reinvest, compound, or roll over.

We say result, daily result, the engine's average daily result. We never say return, R O I, yield, interest, or dividend; those words are retired. We say average, on average, at the average daily result. We never say guaranteed, fixed, every day you get, or you will earn: days vary from zero to several percent, and nothing is guaranteed, so we say average every time a rate or a date appears. We say commission, the Momentum Plan, the base matrix, the breakage differential. We never say passive income, residual, bonus pool, or recruitment bonus: commission is a share of what a contract earned that day, never of a purchase, and nobody is paid for recruiting.

We say the contract's daily earnings, the module's result. We never say the company pays you, or profit share from the company: the money is trading profit the engine made that day, split fifty, twenty-five, twenty-five. We say AI trading engine, Delta One engine, software as a service, written A I and spoken A I. We never say fund, scheme, program, or platform. We say most members earn no commission at all. We never say typical results, or average earnings of members. And we say Delta One or the DAO Treasury, never the Treasury's internal positions: commission no member qualifies for stays with Delta One.

Delta_One_Language_Card.find: Seven things that end a distributorship
Delta_One_Language_Card.text: Seven things that end a distributorship. Promising, implying or guaranteeing any result, rate or date. Calling a module a deposit, an investment, a fund or an account, or calling results returns, interest or yield. Quoting a figure that is not in a published Delta One document, or quoting one without the word average. Showing anyone's earnings as typical, or recruiting with your own statement. Presenting Delta One as a bank, a regulated fund, a government-backed product, or as risk-free. Advertising on social media without the disclosure line and the draft status until compliance has signed off. Mentioning the Treasury's internal positions or anything from partner-only documents. The test before you send anything: does it say average? Does it say not guaranteed? Does it say purchase, not deposit? Would compliance sign it? If any answer is no, do not send it.

Delta_One_Rewards_Disclosure_Statement.text: This is Aria. I will read you the Rewards Disclosure Statement: what members earn from the Momentum Plan. Read it before you decide, and give it to every person you introduce. Most members earn no commission at all. In Delta One's own model of a ten thousand member organization, seventy-nine percent of members hold no rank and receive nothing from the plan; they receive only their own module's results. Commission depends on building and keeping an organization, on the line balance rule, and on the engine actually making a profit on the day.

The model, not a promise. The figures on this page come from a simulated organization of ten thousand members, every member with an active module, ranks assigned by the published rules, at the engine's average daily result of half a percent a day. They are arithmetic, not experience: Delta One has no operating history to report, and when it does, this page will carry the real figures instead. In the model, seven thousand nine hundred and forty-four members, seventy-nine percent, are unranked and earn zero. About thirteen percent reach Fuji, with an average commission of three hundred and ninety-eight USDT a month. About five percent reach Kilimanjaro, at one thousand two hundred and seventy-three USDT a month. Just over one percent reach Matterhorn; half a percent reach Denali; five members in ten thousand reach Rainier; three reach K two; and nobody reaches Everest.

Delta_One_Rewards_Disclosure_Statement.find: What is not in these numbers
Delta_One_Rewards_Disclosure_Statement.text: What the numbers mean. Commission is a share of what the modules in your organization earned that day from trading, never a share of what anyone paid. A day without trading profit pays nobody. Rank is rechecked at every 12:00 UTC settlement and needs three things at once. The averages hide the spread: within a rank, members with balanced lines earn more and members with one heavy line earn less. Your own module's results are not commission and are not in this table. What is not in these numbers: any cost of building, days with no profit and periods with a lower average, and tax. Results and rewards are not guaranteed by Delta One, a bank or any government scheme. A module is a software purchase; the purchase price is not refundable and can be lost. Only purchase with money you can afford to lose.

Delta_One_Module_Product_Guide.text: This is Aria. I will read you the Module Product Guide: everything about a module, in order. Delta One is an AI trading engine: software that looks for the right trade opportunities and the right way to trade them, across arbitrage, high-frequency and leveraged strategies. It is sold as software as a service, in modules. A module is your purchase of the engine for the amount you choose, from one thousand USDT; the engine does all the trading. Every day the engine makes a trading result, your module receives its share, until the module has delivered two times the amount you put in. Then it ends. Three things to understand first: results come only from trading results, and a day with no profit pays nothing; the amount you put in is not paid back separately, the two times is everything a module will ever deliver; and when a module reaches two times it ends, and to keep earning you buy a new one.

How a day works. The engine trades on all approved venues, all day. Before settlement, the day's result is confirmed against the exchange statements; zero or a loss means nothing is credited to anyone. At settlement the result is split fifty, twenty-five, twenty-five: half to members as their daily result, a quarter to the compensation plan, a quarter to the DAO Treasury. Your module's share of the members' half is in proportion to its size, on average half a percent of the module. At twelve noon UTC your result is settled: it opens a rebuy module, or lands in your app wallet. A new module starts earning from the day after its purchase is confirmed.

Your first eleven days. For the first ten calendar days every result is automatically rebought: each day's result opens a new, small rebuy module with its own two-times life, so your results start earning results. On day eleven you choose: withdraw that day's result, or leave the switch on. From day twelve your Auto-Rebuy switch decides every day. In the worked example, a ten thousand USDT module at the average makes fifty USDT on day one, which opens rebuy module one; by day ten, about five hundred and eleven USDT of results are at work in ten rebuy modules alongside the original ten thousand.

The switch, in plain words. On: each day's result opens a new rebuy module and starts earning the next day; good for letting results compound. Off: each day's result lands in your app wallet in USDT; withdraw any time from five USDT, or buy a module from it. You can change the switch any day from day eleven. Rebuy modules can be any size, and they count as new volume for the member who introduced you. The Believer: a member who commits to keeping Auto-Rebuy on for a module's entire life, and the module then delivers two hundred and twenty percent instead of two hundred. The choice is binding: the switch cannot be turned off until the module has delivered its two hundred and twenty. On ten thousand USDT at the average, a standard module ends at twenty thousand around day four hundred; a Believer's at twenty-two thousand around day four hundred and forty.

Examples, at the average daily result with the switch off. A one thousand USDT module: five USDT a day, one hundred and fifty USDT per thirty days, two thousand USDT over its life, one thousand of rewards after your money back. Ten thousand USDT: fifty a day, fifteen hundred per thirty days, twenty thousand in total. Fifty thousand USDT: two hundred and fifty a day, seven thousand five hundred per thirty days, one hundred thousand in total. With Auto-Rebuy on, the capital at work grows and later results are larger, but every module and every rebuy module still ends at its own two times, and nothing is paid on a day without a trading result. Illustrations only. You can hold more than one module, and introducing others is optional.

Delta_One_Module_Product_Guide.find: Purchases, the App Wallet and Withdrawals
Delta_One_Module_Product_Guide.text: Your money. USDT on BNB Smart Chain only, for purchases and withdrawals; USDT on any other network is not credited. After identity checks you send USDT to your personal payment address, and the module is confirmed once the transfer has enough confirmations. The capital is held in Delta One's custody wallets under multi-signature control and moved only to approved trading accounts for the engine. Settlement is every day at twelve noon UTC, and your dashboard shows each day's trading result and each module's running total. Results with the switch off land in the app wallet; withdraw any time, five USDT minimum, sent instantly to your registered wallet, gas fee deducted. No fees except gas. A module cannot be cancelled before two times. Every settlement and withdrawal has an on-chain transaction.

What could go wrong. Trading can lose money, and long losing periods could mean no results for months. Half a percent a day is an average, and the average can fall; it is not guaranteed. The amount you put in is not guaranteed and is not paid back separately; you may lose some or all of it. Your capital cannot be taken out before the module reaches two times, however long that takes. Exchanges, custodians or BNB Smart Chain can fail, freeze funds or be hacked. USDT could lose its one-to-one value. A regulator could restrict or stop the product. Plans that pay for introducing others depend on continued growth, and most participants earn no commission. Taxes can reduce what you keep. Before you buy: read the Key Facts and the member terms, ask any question you have, and only use money you can afford to lose entirely.

All the rules in one place. A purchase of the Delta One AI trading engine, software as a service, not a deposit; the purchase price is not refundable. Minimum one thousand USDT, any amount above, several modules allowed. Daily result: the module's share of half of the day's gross trading result, on average half a percent. A loss day: no result. Maximum: two times the amount put in, that amount included, then the module ends; two point two times for a Believer. First result at the settlement after the day the purchase is confirmed. Days one to ten auto-rebuy; day eleven you may withdraw; from day twelve the switch decides. App wallet: withdraw any time, five USDT minimum, instant, gas deducted. Settlement at twelve noon UTC every day. No cancellation before two times. The compensation plan is optional, paid from the plan's twenty-five percent share, daily, and most members earn none.

Delta_One_Module_FAQ.text: This is Aria. I will read you the Member FAQ: the questions members ask, with short answers. What is a module? Your purchase of the Delta One AI trading engine for the amount you choose, from one thousand USDT; a software product, not a deposit. Your module receives its share of each day's result until it has delivered two times your amount. The minimum is one thousand USDT per module, and you can hold several. Which network? USDT on BNB Smart Chain only. When does my module start earning? From the settlement on the day after your purchase is confirmed. Do I have to recruit anyone? No. Holding a module and introducing others are separate.

Results. How much will I earn? Nobody can promise a figure. The engine's average daily result is half a percent of your module, five USDT a day on one thousand, on average; some days produce nothing, others several percent, and real results may be lower or zero. Is the result guaranteed? No. Why two times? A module is designed to deliver a fixed total of two times your amount; that limits how long each module runs and is what lets the engine keep paying new members. When do I get my money back? It comes back as part of the two times; at the average, after about two hundred days, and everything after that is rewards. Does my module compound? Not by itself: results compound through rebuy modules, automatically for the first ten days, then whenever your switch is on. On a losing day you receive nothing.

Auto-Rebuy and the wallet. In the first ten days each day's result automatically opens a small rebuy module, which earns from the next day. Day eleven is the first day you can take a result out. The switch: on, each day's result opens a rebuy module; off, each day's result lands in your app wallet in USDT; change it any day from day eleven. A Believer commits to keeping Auto-Rebuy on for a module's entire life, and the module then delivers two hundred and twenty percent instead of two hundred; a Believer cannot change their mind until the module has delivered its two hundred and twenty. How do I withdraw? From the app wallet, any time, five USDT minimum, sent instantly, gas fee deducted. Can I buy a module from my wallet? Yes, from one thousand USDT. Do rebuy modules have a minimum? No; any size, each with its own two times.

Your money. Where is it held? In Delta One's custody wallets under multi-signature control, moved only to approved trading accounts for the engine. Can I withdraw my capital early? No; a module runs until it reaches two times and cannot be cancelled; only results can be withdrawn. Are there fees? None, except the network gas fee on withdrawals. What happens when my module reaches two times? It ends; results stop, and any remaining balance stays with the DAO Treasury; rebuy modules keep running to their own two times.

Risks and help. Can I lose money? Yes. You can lose some or all of the money you put in. Is this regulated? Products like this are regulated in many countries; the member terms name the contracting entity, and you should check that the product is permitted where you live. Do I owe tax? Possibly; tax depends on your country, so get your own advice. Who do I contact? Member support through your dashboard, or speak to an agent on Zoom. This FAQ summarises the product; the member terms decide. Every figure is an illustration at the engine's average daily result, not a guarantee, and capital is at risk.
